entities.summary:
The Battle of Yalu River was a pivotal conflict in 1904, marking a decisive clash between Japanese and Russian forces. The battle, fought on April 30, 1904, resulted in a crushing defeat for the Russian naval fleet, dealing a significant blow to their presence in East Asia.

The strategic victory for Japan would have far-reaching consequences, ultimately contributing to their emergence as a major world power. The battle showcased the growing naval dominance of Japan, which would go on to shape the course of the Russo-Japanese War.

The legacy of the Battle of Yalu River can be seen in the subsequent Treaty of Portsmouth, which brought an end to the war and resulted in Japan gaining control of key territories, including the southern half of the island of Sakhalin. This marked a significant turning point in the complex history of the region, with Japan's power and influence becoming increasingly prominent.

The battle would also have a profound impact on the development of the world's naval powers, with the Japanese victory serving as a catalyst for the growth of naval modernization across the globe, particularly in East Asia.
